professions.label: Financial Advisor
professions.description: Financial planning, investing, tax, retirement, insurance and budgeting.
professions.contextHint: Region, instruments, goals, risk profile and time horizon.
professions.customContextPlaceholder: e.g. ₹1.2L monthly income, home loan EMI ₹35k, 2 dependants
professions.descriptionPlaceholder: e.g. I am 34, earn ₹18L a year, have ₹6L in savings and a ₹25k monthly SIP. I want to retire by 55 and fund my daughter’s education in 12 years. Build a plan.
professions.contextPlaceholder: Age, income, expenses, existing investments and loans, dependants, tax bracket…
guardrails: Provide educational guidance, not personalised regulated investment, tax or legal advice; say when a licensed professional should be consulted.
Never guarantee returns; state that past performance does not predict future results and quantify risk where you can.
Apply the rules of the person’s jurisdiction and flag any tax or regulatory rule that may have changed recently.
Do not invent product names, interest rates or figures; label every estimate and assumption.
professions.constraintsPlaceholder:
Monthly investment must stay under ₹30,000
No exposure to crypto
professions.successPlaceholder:
Shows the monthly SIP needed for each goal
Every projection states its return and inflation assumptions

professions.label: Ayurveda Expert

professions.contextHint: Dosha, season, diet, life stage and preferred modalities.
professions.customContextPlaceholder: e.g. desk job, sleeps at 1 am, lives in a humid climate

professions.contextPlaceholder: Age, symptoms and how long, current medication, sleep, digestion, climate, daily schedule…
guardrails: Complement, never replace, medical diagnosis or treatment; never advise stopping prescribed medication.
List red-flag symptoms that need prompt medical attention.
Flag contraindications and possible herb–drug interactions; take extra care with pregnancy, breastfeeding, children, older adults and chronic conditions.
Distinguish classical Ayurvedic principles from what modern clinical evidence supports.
Recommend consulting a qualified Ayurvedic practitioner before starting herbal formulations or Panchakarma.
professions.constraintsPlaceholder:
No dairy (lactose intolerant)
Routine must fit a 9-to-6 office job
professions.successPlaceholder:
Meals use ingredients from an Indian kitchen
Each herb lists who should avoid it

taskTypes.label: Implement a feature
taskTypes.instruction: Design and implement the requested functionality end-to-end.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. Add a password-reset flow: user requests a reset by email, receives a single-use link valid for 30 minutes, and sets a new password. Must integrate with our existing UserService.
checklist: Where it fits in the existing code

taskTypes.label: Code / design review
taskTypes.instruction: Review the provided material critically. Identify issues, rank them by severity, and propose concrete fixes.
taskTypes.placeholder: Paste the code, PR diff or design to review, then say what kind of feedback you want (correctness, security, readability…).
checklist: What it is supposed to do

taskTypes.label: Debug an issue
taskTypes.instruction: Diagnose the root cause of the problem described. Form hypotheses, explain how to verify each, then propose a fix.
taskTypes.placeholder:
e.g. POST /orders returns 500 intermittently under load.
Error: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading "id") at OrderService.create (order.service.ts:42)
Expected: 201 with the order. Actual: 500 roughly 1 in 50 requests.

taskTypes.label: Refactor
taskTypes.instruction: Refactor the provided code to improve readability, structure and maintainability without changing its external behaviour.
taskTypes.placeholder: Paste the code to refactor and explain what bothers you about it (long functions, duplication, hard to test…).

taskTypes.label: System / solution design
taskTypes.instruction: Produce a solution design covering components, responsibilities, data flow, interfaces and key trade-offs.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. Design a notification service that sends email, SMS and push to 2M users per day, with user preferences, retries and delivery tracking.

taskTypes.label: API design
taskTypes.instruction: Design a clean, consistent, versionable API including endpoints/operations, request and response shapes, errors and auth.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. Design a REST API for managing subscriptions: create, upgrade/downgrade plans, cancel, and list invoices. Consumers are our web app and partners.

taskTypes.label: Optimise performance
taskTypes.instruction: Identify performance bottlenecks, explain their impact, and propose measurable optimisations in priority order.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. The /reports endpoint takes 4–6 s at p95. It runs 3 SQL queries over a 20M-row table. Target: under 500 ms.

taskTypes.label: Write tests
taskTypes.instruction: Write a thorough, maintainable test suite covering the happy path, edge cases and failure modes.
taskTypes.placeholder: Paste the code under test and say which framework to use and what level of tests you want (unit, integration, E2E).

taskTypes.label: Write documentation
taskTypes.instruction: Write clear, well-structured documentation tailored to the target audience.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. Write a README for our internal CLI that deploys preview environments. Readers are new engineers in their first week.

taskTypes.label: Explain a concept
taskTypes.instruction: Explain the concept clearly, building from fundamentals to practical application, with concrete examples.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. Explain how database isolation levels work and when to use each, with PostgreSQL examples.

taskTypes.label: Migration plan
taskTypes.instruction: Produce a safe, incremental migration plan with phases, risks, rollback strategy and validation steps.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. Migrate our monolith’s user module from MySQL 5.7 to PostgreSQL 16 with zero downtime. ~40 tables, 300 GB.

taskTypes.label: UI / UX design
taskTypes.instruction: Design the interface: layout, hierarchy, components, states and interactions, with rationale for each decision.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. Design the onboarding flow for a B2B analytics app: account setup, connecting a data source, and the first dashboard. Users are non-technical managers.

taskTypes.label: Compare options
taskTypes.instruction: Compare the candidate options objectively against relevant criteria and give a clear recommendation.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. Compare Kafka, RabbitMQ and AWS SQS for our order-event pipeline (~5k msg/s, ordering per customer, small team).

taskTypes.label: Financial plan
taskTypes.instruction: Build a goal-based financial plan: cash flow, emergency fund, protection, investments per goal and a review schedule.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. 34, ₹18L income, ₹6L savings. Goals: retire at 55, daughter’s education in 12 years, buy a home in 5 years. Build a plan.

taskTypes.label: Portfolio review
taskTypes.instruction: Review the portfolio for allocation, diversification, overlap, cost, risk and fit with the goals, then propose specific changes in priority order.
taskTypes.placeholder: Paste your holdings (fund/stock, amount, since when) and say what the money is for.

taskTypes.label: Compare investments
taskTypes.instruction: Compare the investment options on return potential, risk, liquidity, cost, tax treatment and suitability, then recommend one for this situation.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. Compare PPF, ELSS and NPS for ₹1.5L a year of tax-saving investment for a 30-year-old in the new vs old tax regime.

taskTypes.label: Tax planning
taskTypes.instruction: Identify legal ways to reduce tax for this situation, quantify the saving of each, and note deadlines and documentation.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. Salaried, ₹24L CTC with HRA, home loan interest ₹2.1L, some capital gains from equity funds this year. Old or new regime, and how to save more?

taskTypes.label: Retirement plan
taskTypes.instruction: Estimate the retirement corpus needed, the gap to current savings, the monthly investment required and a withdrawal strategy, stating all assumptions.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. 40 years old, ₹80k monthly expenses today, ₹45L invested, want to retire at 58. How much do I need and how do I get there?

taskTypes.label: Budget & debt plan
taskTypes.instruction: Create a realistic monthly budget and a debt repayment plan (avalanche or snowball) with a timeline to become debt-free.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. Take-home ₹95k. Credit card debt ₹2.4L at 36%, car loan ₹4L at 9%. Expenses are ~₹70k. Help me budget and clear debt.

taskTypes.label: Insurance needs
taskTypes.instruction: Assess life, health and other insurance needs, recommend cover amounts and policy types, and point out gaps or over-insurance.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. Married, one child, ₹20L income, home loan ₹40L outstanding, employer health cover ₹5L. What insurance do I need?

taskTypes.label: Explain a concept
taskTypes.instruction: Explain the financial concept clearly, from fundamentals to practical use, with a worked numeric example.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. Explain XIRR vs CAGR and when each is the right measure for my SIP returns.

taskTypes.label: Prakriti / dosha assessment
taskTypes.instruction: Assess the likely Prakriti (constitution) and current Vikriti (imbalance) from the details given, explain the reasoning, and list the questions that would confirm it.
taskTypes.placeholder: Describe your body frame, skin, digestion, sleep, energy, temperament, and what aggravates you (cold, heat, heavy food…).

taskTypes.label: Diet & meal plan
taskTypes.instruction: Design an Ayurvedic diet (Ahara) for this constitution and season: foods to favour and reduce, meal timing, and a sample day of meals.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. Pitta-dominant, acidity and irritability in summer, vegetarian, works long hours. Create a diet plan.

taskTypes.label: Daily & seasonal routine
taskTypes.instruction: Create a Dinacharya (daily routine) and Ritucharya (seasonal adjustments) suited to the constitution and lifestyle, with practical timings.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. I wake at 8, work 10–7 at a desk, eat dinner at 10 pm and sleep at 1 am. Help me build a balanced routine for the coming winter.
checklist: What you are willing to change

taskTypes.label: Support for a health concern
taskTypes.instruction: Explain the concern from an Ayurvedic perspective (dosha, Agni, Ama), then give diet, lifestyle, yoga and herbal support, clearly marking what needs medical evaluation.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. Recurring migraines for 2 years, worse in summer and with skipped meals. On sumatriptan as needed. What can Ayurveda offer alongside?

taskTypes.label: Herbs & home remedies
taskTypes.instruction: Recommend suitable herbs or kitchen remedies with preparation, dosage range, timing (Anupana), duration and contraindications.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. What herbs or home remedies can help with mild seasonal cough and congestion for an adult? I take blood-pressure medication.

taskTypes.label: Detox / Panchakarma plan
taskTypes.instruction: Outline a safe home-based seasonal cleanse or explain which Panchakarma therapies suit this person, with preparation (Purvakarma), main procedure and recovery (Paschatkarma).
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. I feel heavy and sluggish after the winter. Is a spring Kapha cleanse right for me, and what would it involve?

taskTypes.label: Yoga & pranayama routine
taskTypes.instruction: Design a yoga, pranayama and meditation routine suited to the dosha and goal, with sequence, durations and modifications.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. 20-minute morning routine to calm Vata anxiety and improve sleep, beginner, mild lower-back stiffness.

taskTypes.label: Explain a concept
taskTypes.instruction: Explain the Ayurvedic concept clearly, with its classical basis, practical meaning and everyday examples.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. Explain Agni and Ama, and how to tell if my digestion is balanced.

taskTypes.label: Goal setting & action plan
taskTypes.instruction: Help clarify the goal, turn it into SMART goals with milestones, identify obstacles and resources, and agree concrete next steps.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. I want to run my own design studio within 2 years but I keep postponing it. Help me set clear goals and a plan.

taskTypes.label: Career transition
taskTypes.instruction: Explore the career change: motivations, transferable strengths, options, risks and a step-by-step transition plan with experiments to test it.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. 8 years as a software engineer, considering product management. Worried about the pay cut and starting over.

taskTypes.label: Build or break a habit
taskTypes.instruction: Design a habit plan using behaviour-science techniques (cues, tiny habits, environment design, tracking) and plan for relapses.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. I want to exercise every morning and stop scrolling my phone in bed. I have tried several times and give up after a week.

taskTypes.label: Make a decision
taskTypes.instruction: Guide the decision: clarify values and criteria, explore options and consequences, surface fears and assumptions, and help reach a choice.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. Should I accept a promotion that requires relocating to another city with my family?

taskTypes.label: Overcome a block
taskTypes.instruction: Identify the limiting belief or block, examine the evidence for and against it, reframe it, and design small experiments to build confidence.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. I never apply for leadership roles because I feel I am not good enough, even though my manager encourages me.

taskTypes.label: Work-life balance
taskTypes.instruction: Assess the current balance across life areas, find the biggest drains and gains, and create a sustainable plan with boundaries.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. I work 55 hours a week, rarely see friends, and feel guilty whenever I rest. I want more balance without hurting my career.
checklist: What balance looks like to you

taskTypes.label: Design a coaching session
taskTypes.instruction: Design a coaching session or programme: objectives, structure, powerful questions, exercises, and follow-up.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. A 60-minute first session with a mid-level manager who wants to improve delegation.

taskTypes.label: Reflection & journaling
taskTypes.instruction: Create a set of reflection or journaling prompts, sequenced to deepen self-awareness and lead to action.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. A 30-day journaling series to discover what I really want from the next 5 years.

taskTypes.label: Training programme
taskTypes.instruction: Design a periodised training programme with weekly structure, exercises, sets, reps, progression and deload weeks.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. 4 days a week at home with dumbbells up to 20 kg, goal fat loss + strength, 12 weeks.

taskTypes.label: Nutrition plan
taskTypes.instruction: Estimate calorie and macronutrient targets and build a practical meal plan with portions, timing and substitutions.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. 29, 78 kg, 175 cm, moderately active, vegetarian, goal fat loss while keeping muscle.

taskTypes.label: Exercise technique
taskTypes.instruction: Explain correct technique, common faults and how to fix them, cues, and safer variations.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. How do I deadlift with correct form? I feel it in my lower back rather than my glutes.

taskTypes.label: Mobility & recovery
taskTypes.instruction: Create a mobility, stretching and recovery routine targeting the problem areas, with progressions.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. Tight hips and hamstrings from sitting 9 hours a day; 15 minutes a day available.

taskTypes.label: Explain a concept
taskTypes.instruction: Explain the training or nutrition concept clearly, with the evidence behind it and practical examples.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. Explain progressive overload and how to apply it with only bodyweight exercises.

taskTypes.label: Business strategy
taskTypes.instruction: Analyse the situation and produce a business strategy: where to play, how to win, priorities, risks and metrics.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. B2B invoicing tool for small manufacturers, 40 customers mostly from referrals. How do we reach 500 customers in 12 months?

taskTypes.label: Go-to-market plan
taskTypes.instruction: Create a go-to-market plan: ideal customer profile, positioning, channels, launch phases, budget split and success metrics.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. Launching a premium Ayurvedic skincare brand online in India with a ₹10L launch budget.

taskTypes.label: Marketing campaign
taskTypes.instruction: Plan a marketing campaign: objective, audience, message, creative concepts, channels, timeline, budget and KPIs.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. Diwali campaign for our D2C tea brand to grow repeat purchases by 20%.

taskTypes.label: Content calendar
taskTypes.instruction: Build a content strategy and calendar: pillars, formats, topics, publishing cadence and how each piece drives the goal.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. 3-month LinkedIn and blog calendar to build authority for a cybersecurity consultancy.

taskTypes.label: Write copy
taskTypes.instruction: Write persuasive, on-brand copy for the specified asset, with variations to test.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. Landing page hero, three benefit blocks and a CTA for a habit-tracking app for students.

taskTypes.label: Market & competitor analysis
taskTypes.instruction: Analyse the market and competitors: segments, size estimates, needs, competitor strengths and weaknesses, and opportunities.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. Analyse the market for online yoga classes for corporate employees in India.

taskTypes.label: Pitch / investor deck
taskTypes.instruction: Outline a compelling pitch: problem, solution, market, traction, business model, competition, team and the ask.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. Seed-round pitch for an AI tutoring app, ₹3 Cr raise, 2,000 paying users.

taskTypes.label: Pricing strategy
taskTypes.instruction: Recommend a pricing model, tiers and price points, with the rationale, expected impact and how to test them.
taskTypes.placeholder: e.g. Pricing for a SaaS scheduling tool for clinics, currently ₹999/month flat.

constraints.label: Production-ready
constraints.instruction: The solution must be production-ready, not a toy example.

constraints.label: Robust error handling
constraints.instruction: Handle errors and edge cases explicitly; never swallow errors silently.

constraints.label: Include tests
constraints.instruction: Include automated tests that cover the main behaviour and key edge cases.

constraints.label: Security best practices
constraints.instruction: Follow security best practices (input validation, least privilege, no secrets in code, OWASP guidance).

constraints.label: Performance-aware
constraints.instruction: Consider performance and scalability; call out time/space complexity where relevant.

constraints.label: Clean code / SOLID
constraints.instruction: Follow clean code and SOLID principles with clear naming and small, focused units.

constraints.label: Accessibility (WCAG AA)
constraints.instruction: Meet WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility requirements (contrast, keyboard access, semantics, focus states).

constraints.label: Minimal dependencies
constraints.instruction: Avoid introducing new third-party dependencies unless clearly justified.

constraints.label: Backward compatible
constraints.instruction: Preserve backward compatibility with existing interfaces and data.

constraints.label: Well commented
constraints.instruction: Comment non-obvious logic and document public interfaces.

constraints.label: Observability
constraints.instruction: Include structured logging, metrics and tracing hooks where appropriate.

constraints.label: Cost-conscious
constraints.instruction: Keep infrastructure and runtime cost in mind and call out cost implications.

constraints.label: Show calculations
constraints.instruction: Show the calculations behind every number, with the assumed return, inflation and tax rates.

constraints.label: Inflation-adjusted
constraints.instruction: Express future amounts in both nominal and inflation-adjusted (today’s money) terms.

constraints.label: Tax-efficient
constraints.instruction: Prefer tax-efficient options and show the post-tax outcome.

constraints.label: Low-cost / passive first
constraints.instruction: Prefer low-cost, diversified, passive instruments unless there is a clear reason not to.

constraints.label: Emergency fund & cover first
constraints.instruction: Make sure the emergency fund and adequate insurance are in place before recommending investments.

constraints.label: Best / base / worst case
constraints.instruction: Show best-, base- and worst-case scenarios for projections.

constraints.label: No product pitching
constraints.instruction: Recommend categories of instruments rather than specific branded products unless asked.

constraints.label: Jurisdiction rules
constraints.instruction: Apply the tax and regulatory rules of the stated country and name the rules you rely on.

constraints.label: Cite classical texts
constraints.instruction: Reference the classical sources (Charaka Samhita, Sushruta Samhita, Ashtanga Hridayam) where relevant.

constraints.label: Note modern evidence
constraints.instruction: Note where modern research supports, contradicts or has not studied a recommendation.

constraints.label: Safety & contraindications
constraints.instruction: State contraindications, herb–drug interactions and who should avoid each recommendation.

constraints.label: Kitchen-friendly
constraints.instruction: Prefer remedies and foods that are easily available in a home kitchen.

constraints.label: Season-aware
constraints.instruction: Adapt recommendations to the current season (Ritucharya) and climate.

constraints.label: Explain Sanskrit terms
constraints.instruction: Explain every Sanskrit term in plain English the first time it appears.

constraints.label: Integrative with modern care
constraints.instruction: Position recommendations as complementary to modern medical care.

constraints.label: Gradual changes
constraints.instruction: Introduce changes gradually, starting with the few that matter most.

constraints.label: Coach with questions
constraints.instruction: Coach mainly through powerful open questions rather than telling the person what to do.

constraints.label: SMART goals
constraints.instruction: Express goals as SMART goals (specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, time-bound).

constraints.label: Tiny first step
constraints.instruction: End with one small first step the person can take within 24 hours.

constraints.label: Accountability plan
constraints.instruction: Include an accountability plan: how progress is tracked, reviewed and celebrated.

constraints.label: Strengths-based
constraints.instruction: Build on the person’s existing strengths and past successes.

constraints.label: Empathetic & non-judgmental
constraints.instruction: Acknowledge feelings and stay non-judgmental throughout.

constraints.label: Evidence-informed
constraints.instruction: Ground techniques in evidence (positive psychology, behaviour science, CBT-informed methods) and name them.

constraints.label: Progressive overload
constraints.instruction: Build in clear progressive overload and deload weeks.

constraints.label: Use only my equipment
constraints.instruction: Use only the equipment listed; give alternatives for anything else.

constraints.label: Time-boxed sessions
constraints.instruction: Keep each session within the stated time, including warm-up and cool-down.

constraints.label: Warm-up & cool-down
constraints.instruction: Include a warm-up and cool-down for every session.

constraints.label: Calories & macros
constraints.instruction: Give calorie and macronutrient targets and show how they were calculated.

constraints.label: Evidence-based
constraints.instruction: Base recommendations on current sports-science evidence and avoid fads.

constraints.label: Injury-safe modifications
constraints.instruction: Give easier and joint-friendly modifications for each exercise.

constraints.label: Data-backed
constraints.instruction: Back recommendations with data or clearly labelled assumptions, and say how to validate them.

constraints.label: Measurable KPIs
constraints.instruction: Define measurable KPIs and targets for every initiative.

constraints.label: Budget-conscious
constraints.instruction: Stay within the stated budget and show how it is allocated.

constraints.label: On-brand voice
constraints.instruction: Match the brand voice and positioning described.

constraints.label: Customer-centric
constraints.instruction: Start from customer needs and pains, not product features.

constraints.label: Quick wins + long term
constraints.instruction: Separate quick wins (next 30 days) from longer-term initiatives.

constraints.label: Ethical & compliant
constraints.instruction: Keep claims truthful and follow advertising, consumer-protection and privacy rules.

reasoning.label: Ask clarifying questions first
reasoning.instruction: If any requirement is ambiguous or missing, ask concise clarifying questions before producing the final answer.

reasoning.label: State assumptions
reasoning.instruction: Explicitly list any assumptions you make.

reasoning.label: Think step by step
reasoning.instruction: Reason through the problem step by step before giving the final answer.

reasoning.label: Offer alternatives & trade-offs
reasoning.instruction: Present at least two viable approaches with their trade-offs, then recommend one and justify it.

reasoning.label: Self-review before answering
reasoning.instruction: Before finalising, review your answer against the requirements and success criteria and fix any gaps.

reasoning.label: Highlight risks
reasoning.instruction: Highlight risks, pitfalls and anything that needs human verification.

reasoning.label: Recommend patterns
reasoning.instruction: Recommend the design patterns and architectural style that best fit this problem, justify each choice, and name patterns you deliberately avoided and why.

reasoning.label: Ask for missing personal details
reasoning.instruction: Recommendations depend on the person’s situation: if important personal details are missing, list what you assumed and what would change the advice.

outputFormats.label: Structured Markdown
outputFormats.instruction: Respond in well-structured Markdown with clear headings, bullet points and fenced code blocks.

outputFormats.label: Summary first
outputFormats.instruction: Start with a 3–5 bullet summary of the key recommendations, then give the details.

outputFormats.label: Code first, brief notes
outputFormats.instruction: Lead with complete, runnable code in fenced blocks, followed by brief explanatory notes.

outputFormats.label: Step-by-step guide
outputFormats.instruction: Respond as a numbered, step-by-step guide that the reader can follow in order.

outputFormats.label: Comparison table
outputFormats.instruction: Use a Markdown table to compare options, followed by a short recommendation.

outputFormats.label: Architecture Decision Record
outputFormats.instruction: Respond as an ADR with sections: Title, Status, Context, Decision, Alternatives Considered, Consequences.

outputFormats.label: Include diagrams (Mermaid)
outputFormats.instruction: Include Mermaid diagrams (in ```mermaid blocks) to illustrate architecture or flows.

outputFormats.label: JSON only
outputFormats.instruction: Respond with valid JSON only, no prose before or after it.

outputFormats.label: Checklist
outputFormats.instruction: Respond as an actionable checklist grouped by category.

outputFormats.label: Action plan
outputFormats.instruction: Include an action plan table with columns: action, why, when, and how progress is measured.

outputFormats.label: Week-by-week plan
outputFormats.instruction: Lay out the plan week by week, showing what changes each week.

outputFormats.label: Daily schedule
outputFormats.instruction: Include a daily schedule with times (for example 6:00 wake up, 6:15 …).

outputFormats.label: Meal plan table
outputFormats.instruction: Include a meal plan table by time of day with portions and simple substitutions.

outputFormats.label: Projection table
outputFormats.instruction: Include a year-by-year projection table (contributions, growth, inflation-adjusted value) with the assumptions stated above it.

outputFormats.label: Allocation table
outputFormats.instruction: Show the recommended asset allocation as a table with percentages and the rationale for each asset class.

outputFormats.label: Worksheet
outputFormats.instruction: Include a short worksheet: reflection questions with space to answer and a closing commitment statement.

outputFormats.label: Workout tables
outputFormats.instruction: Present each workout as a table: exercise, sets, reps or time, rest, and form notes.

outputFormats.label: Slide outline
outputFormats.instruction: Respond as a slide-by-slide outline: slide title, key message and supporting points.

audiences.label: Me (experienced engineer)
audiences.instruction: The reader is an experienced engineer: skip basics and be precise.

audiences.label: Junior developer
audiences.instruction: The reader is a junior developer: explain the reasoning and define jargon.

audiences.label: Engineering team
audiences.instruction: The reader is an engineering team: be precise and actionable.

audiences.label: Non-technical stakeholders
audiences.instruction: The reader is non-technical: avoid jargon and focus on impact, cost and risk.

audiences.label: Me (individual investor)
audiences.instruction: The reader is an individual investor managing their own money: be practical and explain trade-offs.

audiences.label: Beginner, no finance background
audiences.instruction: The reader is new to personal finance: define every term and use simple numeric examples.

audiences.label: Family / couple
audiences.instruction: The readers are a family planning together: address shared goals and each person’s role.

audiences.label: High-net-worth individual
audiences.instruction: The reader is a high-net-worth individual: cover tax efficiency, estate planning and advanced instruments.

audiences.label: Small business owner
audiences.instruction: The reader owns a small business: separate business and personal finances and cover cash-flow risk.

audiences.label: Fellow advisor
audiences.instruction: The reader is a finance professional: be technical and precise.

audiences.label: Me (general wellbeing)
audiences.instruction: The reader wants to improve their own wellbeing: be practical and easy to follow.

audiences.label: New to Ayurveda
audiences.instruction: The reader is new to Ayurveda: introduce concepts gently and avoid unexplained jargon.

audiences.label: Parent (for a child)
audiences.instruction: The reader is a parent asking about a child: use child-appropriate guidance and doses, and be extra cautious.

audiences.label: Older adult
audiences.instruction: The reader is an older adult: consider medications, mobility and gentler practices.

audiences.label: Practitioner / student
audiences.instruction: The reader is an Ayurveda practitioner or student: use classical terminology and cite sources.

audiences.label: Me (the coachee)
audiences.instruction: The reader is the person being coached: speak to them directly.

audiences.label: Working professional
audiences.instruction: The reader is a busy working professional: keep exercises short and practical.

audiences.label: Student / young adult
audiences.instruction: The reader is a student or young adult: relate examples to studies and early career.

audiences.label: Team / group
audiences.instruction: The audience is a team or group: include group exercises and shared commitments.

audiences.label: A coach preparing a session
audiences.instruction: The reader is a coach preparing a session: include facilitator notes and timing.

audiences.label: Beginner
audiences.instruction: The reader is a beginner: explain exercises simply and start conservatively.

audiences.label: Intermediate
audiences.instruction: The reader trains regularly: use standard training terminology.

audiences.label: Athlete
audiences.instruction: The reader is an athlete: be specific about periodisation and performance metrics.

audiences.label: Older adult
audiences.instruction: The reader is an older adult: prioritise balance, joint health and safety.

audiences.label: Trainer designing for a client
audiences.instruction: The reader is a trainer: include coaching cues and progression rules.

audiences.label: Founder / small team
audiences.instruction: The reader is a founder with a small team: prioritise ruthlessly and keep it executable.

audiences.label: Marketing / sales team
audiences.instruction: The readers are a marketing or sales team: be specific and actionable.

audiences.label: Executives / board
audiences.instruction: The readers are executives: lead with impact, numbers and decisions needed.

audiences.label: Investors
audiences.instruction: The readers are investors: emphasise market, traction, economics and risks.

audiences.label: Customers
audiences.instruction: The output is customer-facing: write in the brand voice for the end customer.

tones.label: Concise
tones.instruction: Be concise and direct. No filler.

tones.label: Detailed
tones.instruction: Be thorough and detailed; completeness matters more than brevity.

tones.label: Mentoring
tones.instruction: Use a supportive, teaching tone and explain the why behind each recommendation.

tones.label: Empathetic
tones.instruction: Use a warm, empathetic and encouraging tone.

tones.label: Formal
tones.instruction: Use a formal, professional tone suitable for documentation.

lengths.label: Short
lengths.instruction: Keep the response short (roughly under 300 words, excluding code).

lengths.label: Medium
lengths.instruction: Aim for a medium-length response (roughly 300–800 words, excluding code).

lengths.label: Long
lengths.instruction: A long, comprehensive response is welcome.

items.label: Factory Method
items.hint: Let subclasses or functions decide which class to instantiate

items.label: Abstract Factory
items.hint: Create families of related objects without naming concrete classes

items.label: Builder
items.hint: Construct complex objects step by step

items.label: Singleton
items.hint: One shared instance; use sparingly

items.label: Prototype
items.hint: Create objects by cloning an existing instance

items.label: Dependency Injection
items.hint: Pass dependencies in rather than creating them inside

items.label: Adapter
items.hint: Make an incompatible interface fit the one you expect

items.label: Decorator
items.hint: Add behaviour by wrapping an object

items.label: Facade
items.hint: Simple interface over a complex subsystem

items.label: Proxy
items.hint: Stand-in that controls access (lazy loading, caching, auth)

items.label: Composite
items.hint: Treat individual objects and trees uniformly

items.label: Bridge
items.hint: Separate an abstraction from its implementation

items.label: Strategy
items.hint: Swap interchangeable algorithms at runtime

items.label: Observer
items.hint: Notify subscribers when state changes

items.label: Command
items.hint: Encapsulate a request as an object (undo, queues)

items.label: State machine
items.hint: Behaviour changes with explicit states and transitions

items.label: Chain of Responsibility

items.label: Template Method
items.hint: Fixed algorithm skeleton with overridable steps

items.label: Mediator

items.label: Visitor
items.hint: Add operations to a structure without changing it

items.label: Layered (N-tier)

items.label: Clean / Hexagonal (Ports & Adapters)

items.label: MVC
